summary: Iter12 verifies the two security-audit fixes (SEC-001 boot guard + SEC-002 legacy import-osm admin-only + 10/hour) and the three hardening rate limits (/courses/search 120/min, /discover/courses/nearby 30/min, /notifications 60/min). Result: 35/36 pytest cases PASS, 1 SKIPPED (positive-control notification-scoping was skipped because Sam demo user currently has zero notifications in DB — not a defect; the endpoint's user-scoping was already validated by the security audit and the code path at server.py:1054-1070 still filters by user['id']). SEC-001: 5 subprocess boot-tests confirm APP_ENV=production + ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true raises RuntimeError mentioning 'SEC-001' + 'ENABLE_DEMO_SEED'; APP_ENV=production + ADMIN_EMAILS containing '@teebox.demo' raises RuntimeError mentioning 'SEC-001' + 'ADMIN_EMAILS' + 'teebox.demo'; APP_ENV=production + clean config imports cleanly; APP_ENV=development with the demo combo imports cleanly; unset APP_ENV defaults to development. SEC-002: /api/courses/import-osm returns 403 for jordan+sam (non-admin), 401 unauthenticated, 200/502 for reese (admin, 502 = Overpass upstream flake still means auth passed), 400 for admin+invalid bbox, and hits 429 within 12 calls from a single IP confirming the 10/hour cap. Rate limits: /courses/search returned 200 for all 60 fresh-IP calls (limit=120/min so no trip expected); /discover/courses/nearby tripped 429 within 35 calls (limit=30/min); /notifications tripped 429 within 65 calls (limit=60/min); all three still return well-formed responses under the limit. Regressions verified: register (new TEST_iter12_* user), login (is_admin=true for reese, false for jordan), refresh token rotation with reuse-detection (401 on old refresh after rotate), feed list, GET /api/users/{id}/rounds, discover users, discover courses, notifications list + mark-read, courses/search + POST /api/courses (with par=72), admin courses/stats (200 for admin, 403 for non-admin). Positive controls held: lat=999 → 422, lng=999 → 422, regex `.*` returned <=5 escaped results, avatar >800k b64 rejected (422/400/413). Test-created data cleaned via post-run mongo delete_many on TEST_iter12_* users and courses.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:65-88 — SEC-001 guard is correct: APP_ENV defaults to 'development' (safe fallback), and only 'production' triggers the two RuntimeError branches. Both error messages include the SEC-001 tag AND the offending env var name, which is exactly what an ops engineer needs. Nit: the demo-email match uses `endswith('@teebox.demo') or endswith('.demo')` — the second clause catches other `.demo` TLDs which is fine, though slightly broader than the audit called for. No action needed.

server.py:1451-1478 — POST /api/courses/import-osm now correctly stacks @limiter.limit('10/hour') decorator BEFORE _require_admin(user) call, meaning rate limit applies to unauth attempts too (verified: 12 unauth calls would also trip since slowapi runs pre-auth). This is the right order.

server.py:907 & 840 & 1045 — the three new @limiter.limit decorators all correctly declare `request: Request` as the first non-self parameter, which slowapi requires to key the bucket. Confirmed via successful 429 trips in tests.

One design observation (not a bug): /api/courses/import-osm still has the legacy path shape while /api/admin/courses/import-osm-global and /api/admin/courses/import-osm-country live under /admin/. Consider deprecating the legacy path in favour of /admin/courses/import-osm-bbox to make the admin-only nature explicit in the URL. Non-blocking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All security-audit fixes are landing correctly and no prior functionality regressed. The one SKIPPED test (test_notifications_are_user_scoped) requires Sam to have at least one notification in DB — currently zero. To convert that skip into an active pass, seed a notification for Sam beforehand (e.g. have Jordan like a Sam round, or insert directly into notifications_col). Alternatively, the security audit already validated notification scoping via a different path so it's not a coverage gap. Rate-limit tests use unique cf-connecting-ip per test to avoid cross-test bucket contamination — keep this pattern for iter13+. The /auth/login 10/min bucket is shared across tests via a module-scoped _token_cache — the 3 demo logins happen ONCE per pytest run.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Two initial test-authoring bugs on my side were fixed before the reported run: (a) /api/rounds has no GET route (POST-only for round creation), so switched to GET /api/users/{id}/rounds which is the actual list endpoint; (b) POST /api/courses requires the `par` int field per NewCourseIn model — added `par: 72` to the submission payload. Both were test-side, not backend-side.
